narratives.Overview:
Split from #4383 later-arc.

## Pain

After #4383 binds `scope:record-approved-scope` at first mint (digest-equality on activate: the record matches the brief's `file_scope` at park), a later change that expands `file_scope` re-demands a human-presence mint. The operator has left. That is mint-mid-build on a setup-created scope, on renewal, not on first mint.

An existence-only activate gate does not catch this: the first digest is still present. Digest-equality refuses activation until a new mint matches the expanded scope. That renewal mint is this issue, not #4383.

## What this is not

- Not #4383 first-mint (promote --batch, print record-approved-scope against pending/, activate digest-equality, C1 skip declined).
- Not #4587 (intent-constraint mint-mid-build).
- Not #4588 (observable-scope mint-mid-build).
- Not emptying file_scope as a back-out.

## Origin

#4383 pain-audit 5688733074 F2: digest binds at the earliest moment; existence-only gate; expansion re-fires the demand mid-build. Recut 5688748342 named expansion-renewal as uncovered residual on that P1.

## 1. The named pain is the existing remint succeeding; this body does not say what to build instead of it — blocks-the-design

Evidence. At this SHA the renewal mint already exists. `evaluate.ts:455-486` fires `self-authorizing-scope-expansion` when a present, path-bound, human-stamped digest no longer equals the live `file_scope`. `remediationForExpansion()` (`:278-298`) tells the operator to remint with `--confirm` and commit that record on the merge base (or a prior PR) before the expansion PR. `content/docs/scope-provenance.md:143-147` is that flow. `tasks/scope.yml:157` already prints `--kind renewed-approval` against an active path. `human-presence-mint.ts` is why that remint cannot run after the operator has left: agent/CI markers refuse. Same-PR self-remint is refused (`:705-722`; test passed). Gate-integrity (`content/docs/gate-integrity.md`) names `file_scope` self-expansion as a gate, not as a product bug to clear by editing the verifier.

The issue body and Stop 1 `5689610059` name that remint as the hole ("That renewal mint is this issue") and give exclusions (not first mint, not emptying `file_scope`) but no carrier: no verb, no moment, no actor, no Bound-remedy list.

Failure mode, concrete. Body-normative ingest. A builder treats "operator has left, remint still demanded" as a defect to close. Cheapest closes that make the warrant sentence false: (a) agent/CI remint after the operator left, which is the #3110 refuse inverted; (b) same-PR rewrite of `.deft/approved-scope/<plan-id>.json` with the expanded brief, which `evaluate.ts:705-722` already calls self-authorization; (c) drop or warn-away `self-authorizing-scope-expansion` so `task check` is green. All three are edits to the gate or its mint, not a product fix under it.

Disposition consequence. This issue cannot bind as next-build until it names the existing remint as the mechanism it keeps or replaces, and picks one human-present carrier that is not that list: operator returns and runs the documented multi-PR remint (already-holding); a second human-presence window before the operator leaves; or a stated superset minted at the first human window. Unattended remint and verifier-edit stay declined in the same text. First-mint digest-equality is not this finding.

## 2. Stop 1 locates the refuse on activate; at this SHA the refuse is merge-time after activate — sharpens-framing

Evidence. Stop 1: "Digest-equality on activate matches the brief's `file_scope` at park" and "digest-equality refuses activation until a new mint matches the expanded scope." Pin-read: `scope-lifecycle.ts` 0 hits; `packages/core/src/scope` 0 hits. `evaluate.ts:394-396` returns null when the xBRIEF is not in the change set, including a live `file_scope` that already drifted (`evaluate.test.ts` "passes when xBRIEF is not modified in the change set", passed). The hard refuse is `verify:scope-provenance` on a modified active brief, which is a merge-chokepoint reader, not `scope:activate`.

The body also calls the same P1 "mint-mid-build on renewal." Mid-build is post-activate. Activate-time refuse and mid-build remint are two moments. Digest-equality at activate, once built, can catch expansion while the brief is still parked. It cannot catch expansion after activate has already succeeded. That second moment is what `evaluate.ts:455-486` already does.

Failure mode. A builder implements an activate-time digest gate (first-mint digest-equality, not this P1) or searches `scope:activate` for a missing refuse and invents one, leaving the merge-time remint untouched — which is the demand the warrant names.

Disposition consequence. Restate P1 as: after a first human mint, a later declared `file_scope` expansion in the implementation change set hard-fails `verify:scope-provenance` and re-demands `scope:record-approved-scope` while the operator is gone. Do not say activate refuses. Finding 1 still has to name the carrier; this finding only fixes the moment.

## 3. "After #4383 binds" is written as a fact; #4383 is open and this SHA has no first-mint bind — sharpens-framing

Evidence. REST: #4383 `state: open`, `status:claimed`. This SHA's activate path has no approved-scope reader (finding 2). Stop 1's causal sentence is future-tense work treated as present.

Failure mode. A #4589 worker at `f2590baf` implements "renewal" against current activate (no digest reader). They either duplicate the unbuilt first-mint work or ship a second copy of `--kind renewed-approval`. Sequencing stays oral.

Disposition consequence. Record #4383 as an open predecessor, not as a bind that already happened. This leftover can be specified now; it cannot assume activate digest-equality exists.

## 4. Declared-scope population — footnote

Setup still MAY collect `file_scope` and must not mint (`content/skills/deft-directive-setup/SKILL.md` plan.acceptance / file_scope polarity at this SHA). Empty current scope without digest is the soft path (`evaluate.ts:408`, `:779-785`). The remint in finding 1 fires on non-empty declared (or newly declared) `file_scope`. No extra disposition if finding 1 names that population.

## Injection / swarm lens

Triggered: authority (who may remint), untrusted worker edits to `file_scope`, shared `.deft/approved-scope/` on the merge base, C1/headless launches with no operator.

The interpolation seam is not new. The printed remint is already constrained by `human-presence-mint.ts` (agent markers, typed `mint`, `--confirm`). The record key is already path-bound (`evaluate.ts:621-626`) and same-PR rewrite is already fail-closed. A #4589 that adds a remint the worker can run after the operator left is the injection: it turns the worker into the minting principal. Keep mint on the human-presence module; do not add a parallel writer. C1 `--autonomous` has no operator at expansion time by construction — the merge-time hard-fail is the control; an advisory "ping the operator" is not a substitute.

## Road not taken

I considered grading this as already-holding documentation: name the multi-PR remint, close. That would retire findings 1–3 as a single "no leftover product."

I did not lean it. The issue is stamped mechanism-shaped and filed as a work leftover of an uncovered residual, not as a close-as-designed note. Treating it as already-holding here would be a parent take, not a critic inventory. The inventory still stands: the remint verb exists; the missing piece is presence at remint time.

## Steelman

The strongest case for the filing. First-mint digest-equality cannot cover a later, legitimate expansion. That is a different moment from park-and-mint, and splitting it onto its own number is honest leftover accounting. A round-1 body that only names pain and exclusions is how residuals get filed before a successor map writes Bound remedy. Asking this post to carry a full carrier is asking the issue to be the build.

That last point is why the split is right and why finding 1 still blocks bind. A mechanism-shaped body that ingest will treat as the next-build contract, with no carrier and with the existing remint described as the hole, is how (a)/(b)/(c) in finding 1 get built. What would flip: a Bound-remedy (or an explicit already-holding disposition) that (1) names merge-time `verify:scope-provenance` + `--kind renewed-approval` as the existing refuse and remint, (2) records #4383 as open predecessor rather than a bind, (3) restates the moment as post-activate expansion, and (4) picks operator-return / pre-leave second human window / stated-superset at the first human window, with unattended remint and verifier-edit declined.

## Verdict

#4589 cannot bind as written. One blocking finding: the warrant names the designed #3145/#3110 remint as work to do, and gives no carrier that is not "let someone mint after the operator left" or "edit the gate" (1). Two sharpening findings: the refuse is merge-time, not activate (2); #4383 has not bound at this SHA (3). The leftover is real as accounting. The product hole is not "there is no renewal mint."
